verdicts.quote: Lightning Experience in a desktop browser. Salesforce mobile app, Lightning Classic, Experience Cloud sites and Slack are out of scope. ... One Apex entry point (`@AuraEnabled`) receives `{message, priorExchanges[]}`
Sharing: n/a: the bot reads no record (PD-4). ... Controller `with sharing`; ... Any future record access must use user-mode operations
Field-level security: n/a: no field is read.
access is granted by one named permission set covering the entry (R-2), the server operation and the use of the credential.
verdicts.missing: Administration (editing configuration, entering the key) is assigned to an 'Org admin' person, with no permission set or named permission defining who may administer.

verdicts.quote: readable only by the user in that page ... the conversation is shown only in the user's page; stored nowhere; logged never
Decision: one synchronous callout per turn with `setTimeout(configured ms)`; the LWC awaits the imperative Apex call ... A full successful turn and a failed turn each perform zero DML statements
verdicts.missing: The callout-after-DML and no-callout-from-trigger constraints are never stated; the design is synchronous rather than asynchronous, and the rule a builder must respect if DML is added is not given.

verdicts.quote: It is never in source, in deployed or retrieved metadata, in configuration records, in any browser payload, in any log or in any error text.
default callout timeout 10 s; configurable per request 1 ms to 120,000 ms; cumulative callout time per transaction capped at 120 s; 100 callouts per transaction.
verdicts.missing: Heap limit is mentioned without a number (GAP-7) and CPU time limit is not named at all.

verdicts.quote: Apex tests cannot make callouts and use `HttpCalloutMock`
The Apex callout targets `callout:<NamedCredentialName>/...`. The base URL lives in the Named Credential.
one synchronous callout per turn with `setTimeout(configured ms)`; the LWC awaits the imperative Apex call and shows a pending state.
Pressing Enter twice quickly, or double-clicking the send control, on one message results in exactly one service call (mock call count 1) and one user message in the transcript.
Concurrency: the platform's limits on concurrent long-running requests are documented to exclude callouts since Winter '20 (search summary); re-verify at plan.
verdicts.missing: No concurrency or capacity limit value is set, and the outcome for a request the platform refuses for concurrency is not stated.

verdicts.quote: AUTH | HTTP 401 or 403 ... UNAVAILABLE | HTTP 500, 502, 503 ... TIMEOUT | `CalloutException` ... `Grok did not answer in time. It may still have processed your message. Retry?`
RATE_LIMIT | HTTP 429 | `Grok is rate limited right now. Try again in a moment.` ... There is no automatic retry.
INVALID_RESPONSE | HTTP 200 with `{"choices":[]}`, with an empty content string ... A pending state never persists past the service's return
verdicts.missing: A truncated reply (e.g. cut off by the output-token limit) is not addressed; only empty, unreadable and timed-out replies are.

verdicts.quote: Message states: sending, answered, failed. Owner: Bot page; transient. ... message text, replies and keys are not written to any record
verdicts.missing: Conversations are deliberately not stored as records; the model identifier and token/usage counts for a turn are recorded nowhere.

verdicts.quote: kept until refresh, New chat, close or navigation; removed with it. No deletion path is needed because nothing is stored.
It contains no Salesforce username, email, user Id, org Id, record data or client metadata, and no identity field of the API.
After 11 completed exchanges, the request for message `q12` contains exchanges 2 to 11 and `q12` ... exchange 1 is absent.
Sending the empty string or `   ` (three spaces) shows the inline message `Enter a message to send.` ... A message of exactly 4,000 characters ... is sent; a message of 4,001 characters is rejected
model ID, system prompt, maximum prompt characters, remembered exchanges, callout timeout and optional maximum output tokens are administrator-editable configuration
verdicts.missing: No off switch for the bot is specified, and admin visibility of failed requests is only via debug logs, not a stated admin view.

verdicts.quote: Justified exclusion: no persistent audit of who asked what, because PD-3/R-11 forbid storing content ... reopen if the org requires audit (GAP-4).
verdicts.missing: No audit record of who asked what and what was answered exists, so there is no audit retention.

verdicts.quote: A production org identity makes the deploy step refuse. ... a production deploy would also need the Apex coverage gate, a development org deploy does not by itself
Hard bounds: callout timeout between 1 ms and 120,000 ms; shipped default 60,000 ms ... the pending state (R-8.1) is shown before the service returns
The chat page is a designed interface, not scaffolding. ... Designed states: empty ..., loading (R-8.1 indicator), error (R-7 failed message with Retry ...), and answered, all distinct.
Deployment is additive: it creates the bot's components and changes nothing unrelated.
